scenario: WIBTA for selling what I receive in my dad's will? | Obligatory "I'm on mobile, so sorry for mistakes." I (22M) have a very large family. Both of my parents have 3 kids from past relationships, and I'm the only child they have together. My dad (71) never divorced his previous wife, but has been with my mom (61) for the past 25 years. My dad is a severe alcoholic and has a bunch of other health problems. So the talk of his will has come up a few times. He owns the house we currently live in, his (separated) wife's house, and a bar that has 2 apartments above it. As of now, his wife's house would remain her's or if she passes, go to their 3 children. The house we live in now, would be split amongst the 4 of us. The bar and the apartments would go solely to me. My mom is worried she won't get anything when he does pass away, so she constantly asks if I'll give her half of the bar. I personally want nothing to do with the bar due it being a cause for my parent's alcoholism. My mom says I should just give it all to her if that's the case. I would ask her to at least buy out my half, but she has been mentally abusive to me for most of my life, and constantly sabotaged anything I've done to try and better my own life. I've recently thought about just selling my quarter of the house to my siblings, and the entire bar to them or anyone else who wants it. WIBTA if I decided to leave my mom out of anything I get from my dad's will?

These skills help you develop resilience, which can benefit you in various areas of life. 2. **Enhances time management and organization**: Coordinating schedules, meal planning, and keeping track of details can help you develop strong time management and organizational skills. You learn to put yourself in their shoes and consider their needs, which can broaden your perspective and help you become a more compassionate person. 4. **Encourages selflessness and prioritization**: As a mother, you often put the needs of your children before your own. This selfless attitude can help you develop a sense of purpose and prioritize what's truly important in life. 5. **Shapes your values and priorities**: Parenting influences your values and priorities, helping you focus on what truly matters. You may find that your priorities shift from personal goals to family-oriented goals, which can lead to a more fulfilling life. 6. **Develops problem-solving skills**: Managing the challenges of parenting requires creative problem-solving. You learn to think critically, find solutions, and make decisions under pressure. 7. **Enhances emotional intelligence**: Parenting helps you develop emotional intelligence by teaching you to recognize, understand, and manage your emotions. This skill is essential for building strong relationships and navigating complex social situations. 8. **Provides a sense of purpose and fulfillment**: Raising children can give you a sense of purpose and fulfillment, as you watch them grow and develop.
